images.title: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar with the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution
images.description: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar seated in the center as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, surrounded by other identified committee members in formal attire.
images.historical_context: Following India's independence, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was appointed Chairman of the Drafting Committee on August 29, 1947. This photograph captures the core committee tasked with drafting the constitutional document that would define the Republic of India. It highlights Ambedkar's central role as the chief architect of the Constitution.

images.title: Dr. Ambedkar presenting the final draft of the Indian Constitution to Dr. Rajendra Prasad
images.description: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, standing on the left, handing over the bound final draft of the Constitution to Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who is seated at the presiding desk.
images.historical_context: On November 25, 1949, Dr. Ambedkar presented the final draft of the Constitution of India to the President of the Constituent Assembly, Dr. Rajendra Prasad. This momentous event marked the completion of the drafting process before the Constitution was formally adopted on November 26, 1949.

images.title: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar during his academic years at Columbia University
images.description: A young Dr. B. R. Ambedkar wearing round spectacles and a suit, sitting in a studio portrait setting.
images.historical_context: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar studied at Columbia University in the City of New York between 1913 and 1916, where he earned his Master's degree and completed research for his PhD in Economics. This period profoundly shaped his intellectual foundation regarding social justice, economics, and democracy.
